differences.writeup_quote: frequency-debiased readouts and centring change the readout itself.

differences.writeup_quote: Contrastive activation addition steers model outputs; generic attitude vectors show null recall effects; frequency-debiased readouts and centring change the readout itself.
differences.what: the write-up's novelty paragraph contrasts the method against three prior approaches (contrastive activation addition, generic attitude vectors, and frequency-debiased/centred readouts); the message's discussion of related work omits the first two entirely and only engages with the readout-centring/FDR line

message_source_quote: This mirrors the FDR paper's finding that deep-rank items are representation-limited, not ranking-limited — so the 0.50 gate isn't reachable by contrast steering on this model/lens/task; a true readout-space prior removal (centring/FDR) would be strictly stronger but is out of scope here.
writeup_source_quote: Contrastive activation addition steers model outputs; generic attitude vectors show null recall effects; frequency-debiased readouts and centring change the readout itself.
rationale: Both documents mention the frequency-debiased-readout/centring line of prior work only as a contrast to the method's own forward-pass-only approach, never as something the method builds on or reproduces, so both sit at the 'names' level rather than 'credits'. The message adds a specific attributed finding ('FDR paper's finding that deep-rank items are representation-limited') to explain the method's ceiling, while dropping the write-up's parallel contrasts with contrastive activation addition and generic attitude vectors, making the difference mixed rather than purely more or less.
